results.note: The bar itself at night: the restored Old Town shophouse with the lit 'COURAGE КУРАЖ' sign over the entrance, a crowd on the street and string lights. It's a professional photo from the bar's own Telegram channel, posted 28 Apr 2026. The channel is titled 'COURAGE / КУРАЖ', and its tagline is the same as the IG bio @courage.phuket. The bar's small 'COURAGE' logo sits at the bottom centre and mostly falls outside a 16:9 crop. 800 px is the largest size the public Telegram preview serves. The old SUB flyer (.png) was deleted. Also considered: the same channel's interior shot of the backlit bar counter (post 496). Rejected: RA venue and flyers (no photo), phangan.events (placeholder), YouTube @BarCouragePhuket (vertical shorts and animated promos), Tripadvisor and Google user photos (not allowed). The Instagram API fails for this business account, so IG posts couldn't be reached.

A real venue photo, not a flyer. It's a straight-on view of the open-sided jungle dance floor at night: the white double-arch DJ booth with the GROOVY TUNES neon sign, a disco ball and lanterns, jungle trees lit purple on both sides, and rugs on a red-lit floor. It's image 8 of 14 in the venue's pinned 'Book your event at Unclave' post (25 Sep 2025); RA lists this account as the venue's website. Unclave's small white logo sits at the bottom-left, and a centred 16:9 crop leaves only its top edge. Cropping slightly above centre (about 40%) hides it fully. The IG CDN link is signed and expires, but the file is saved locally. Rejected: the old dated RA flyer (deleted), the post's first image (an 'AVAILABLE FOR BOOKING' text collage), Groovy Tunes posts (portrait video covers), the empty Groovy Tunes Telegram channel and the empty RA venue photo field.

No watermark. It's Wat Karon (Wat Suwan Khiri Khet), the temple whose grounds hold the market: the red-and-gold ordination hall with its long green naga balustrade on a blue stone base, palms and hills behind. It's the same building as the old watermarked phuket101 photo, seen from the side. Daytime, slightly overcast (Aug 2011), sharp, 3:2, so a 16:9 crop only trims sky and lawn. The NC licence is fine for a personal guide. No free-licensed photo of the market itself exists. Every 'Karon Temple Market' photo on Flickr is all-rights-reserved (Jamie Monk, ashleyarthur30, Alex Milazzo, Mika Vallineva), and all 8 phuket101 market photos carry ©WillyThuan. Commons only has 'Karon Tempel - panoramio' (actually Wat Chalong) and Alexander Baranov's CC BY 2.0 street shot of the temple gate on Patak Road with market tents (busy with wires). That shot is the fallback if a market hint matters more than looks: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:File_by_Alexander_Baranov_-_._(8500768859).jpg

No watermark, free licence, landscape (almost 16:9). It shows the Koh Sirey monkey viewing point: macaques on the mangrove mudflat beside the island road at about 17:00 (Flickr title 'Les singes de 17 h 00. Ko Sire.', Mar 2014). Sharp, but backlit, with some litter on the mud. It doesn't show the temple or the sea-gypsy village, because no usable free or official photo of those exists. Commons has nothing for Koh Sirey: its 'Wat Ko Si Re' category holds Nai Harn photos, and geotagged files nearby are other places. The only CC photo of the hilltop temple is a portrait, and a 16:9 crop cuts its subject (hnmntn, CC BY-NC 2.0, golden hamsa pillar above the naga stairs: https://www.flickr.com/photos/193313739@N02/53120088126/). phuket101 photos are watermarked. No official or TAT page photo was found. Heads-up for the guide text: Thai news clips from about a year ago (ThaiPBS, Ch7) report that the temple's golden-rock (Kyaiktiyo) replica was closed after a landslide damaged its pavilion. That is the subject of the old photo, so check that it has reopened.

The cafe's own photo, with no watermark: the hillside deck with wooden low tables, floor cushions and a cushioned bench, looking down on a turquoise bay full of anchored yachts, framed by tree branches. It's image 3 of 20 in the cafe's pinned garden-and-sea-view post (3 Mar 2026). It's portrait (1080x1262), but I checked a centred 16:9 crop: it keeps the yachts and the deck tables and cushions. The IG CDN link is signed and expires, but the file is saved locally. Facebook (facebook.com/summoreday) only shows the logo, a portrait interior cover and recent food posts. Rejected: the old '© Phuket 101' photo (deleted), the post's first image (a 'SUM MORE DAY' text overlay) and a sunset sofa shot with children in front. Fallback from the same post: image 2, the open deck with cushion rows facing the bay between two headlands (also portrait).

The hotel itself, as asked: the white Sino-Portuguese shophouse facade at 56 Krabi Road. It shows the red 'SHUNLI HOSTEL' sign with its phone number, the arched balconies, and the black-and-gold 順利 (Shunli) signboard with house number 56 over the entrance. Sharp, bright, 3:2, and a centred 16:9 crop keeps both signs. It's from the property's own gallery on Booking.com ('Shunli Hotel - SHA Extra Plus', 75 photos), not a guest upload. There's no official website, and the Facebook page (Shunlihostelphuket) only shows its sign logo to visitors who aren't logged in. Alternatives from the same gallery: the entrance with open doors under the 順利 sign (id 107324272), the lobby (107324279) and rooms (380493360). The old Thalang Road area photo was replaced.

The shopfront, from the company's own About Us page: a big green 'Mamy Exchange' sign with 'CURRENCY EXCHANGE / ОБМЕН ВАЛЮТ / 外币兑换', the glass storefront and steps, and the 'Mamy Booking / Mamy Exchange Co., Ltd.' pylon beside it. It's the company's only office (9/10 Moo 4, Koh Kaew, on the airport road). Daylight, sharp, 4:3, and a centred 16:9 crop keeps the whole sign. Found through the site's WordPress media library. The homepage og:image is only the SVG logo, and the other uploads are banners or flags.
